info.bio: Alanis Morissette (Ottawa, 1 de junio de 1974) es una cantautora, actriz y productora canadiense, nacionalizada estadounidense. Está posicionada como una de los artistas con mayores ventas en la historia, debido en gran parte a su tercer álbum, "Jagged Little Pill", siendo este el álbum debut más vendido de toda la historia y uno de los álbumes más vendidos de la historia por parte de una artista femenina. Totalizando todos sus álbumes ha superado la barrera de 60 millones de ediciones vendidas en todo el mundo.

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Las mujeres tienen sus propios estilos, en plural: Azalia Snail y su psicodelia lo-fi, Jarboe, Lida Husik (entre la cantante pop y la pintora sonora), Robin Holcomb, Lisa Germano (Geek The Girl, «un viaje dantesco a la psique de una chica»), Tori Amos, Juliana Hatfield, Kristin Hersh, Jewel, Natalie Merchant, Cat Power (Moon Pix), Edith Frost, Lauryn Hill, Shannon Wright. Las «grrrls» más airadas: Lois Maffeo, Ani DiFranco, PJ Harvey (Dry, Rid Of Me), Liz Phair (Exile In Guyville), DQE, Aimee Mann, Sheryl Crow, Alanis Morissette, Neko Case. Y los paisajes sonoros de Björk, la cantautora más influyente de la década, Kate St John, Natacha Atlas, Heather Duby, Solex y Beth Orton.

podcast.title: Career Reinvention with "You Oughta Know" (1995)
podcast.body: The highly effective kiss-off track "You Oughta Know" "single-handedly reinvented Morissette's career," transforming her "from a Canadian pop princess into a truth-telling alternative rock star." This song showcased a powerful, unvarnished emotionality that resonated with a wide audience. "In any case, it's a very effective kiss off to some former lover that single-handedly reinvented Morissette's career, turning her from a Canadian pop princess into a truth-telling alternative rock star."

podcast.title: Artistic Comparison (1990s)
podcast.body: Alanis Morissette was cited as an example of an artist, along with Liz Phair and Courtney Love, who could be "contained and marketed and categorized," in contrast to Sinead O'Connor, whose intensity and uncompromising nature made her difficult to fit into such frameworks. "Unlike, say, Alanis Morissette, Liz Fair, Courtney Love, and a few others, Shanade could never be contained and marketed and categorized."

podcast.title: Biggest Selling Female Album
podcast.body: Alanis Morissette released an album that achieved the distinction of being the biggest selling album from a female artist of all time. This landmark success solidified her global superstar status during the 1990s, contributing to the international recognition of Canadian talent. "Alannis Morissette had the biggest selling album from a female artist of all time."

podcast.body: Alanis Morissette is recognized as one of the artists from previous generations who contributed to Canada's music export success. "Alannus Morse at Sarah McLaughlin, Celine Dion, Shania Twain, Rush, the Guests Who, and dozens and dozens and dozens of others."

podcast.title: Early Career and Producers
podcast.body: Her first two albums were produced by Leslie Howe, a Canadian producer, before her significant reinvention for *Jagged Little Pill*. "it could have been Matt LaBlanc from France, or it's Leslie Howe, the Canadian producer, who was behind her first two albums."

podcast.title: Encouraging Taylor Hawkins to Join Foo Fighters
podcast.body: During their time on summer festivals, Alanis Morissette noticed Taylor Hawkins' connection with the Foo Fighters. She eventually asked him directly when he was going to quit her band and join them, foreshadowing his move to the Foo Fighters. "It got to the point where Alannis asked, when are you just going to quit and join the food fighters?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influential Figure
podcast.body: Alanis Morissette is considered one of the most important alt-rock figures of the 1990s and one of the most influential female singers in music history, inspiring thousands of female musicians. It is suggested that her album *Jagged Little Pill* would have been strongly associated with the #MeToo movement had it existed in 1995. "Do I need to go on about how Alannas Morris said is one of the most important alt rock figures in the 90s? Or should we just go ahead and say that she's one of the most influential female singers in the history of music period?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Maintaining Presence in Grunge Era
podcast.body: Despite the overwhelming focus on guitar music during the grunge era, acts like Alanis Morissette (referred to as "Alannis Moore said") still maintained a primary focus, indicating that not all alternative music was completely squeezed out.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Partnership with Glen Ballard
podcast.body: Despite her previous commercial failures, Alanis's publishing company demonstrated faith in her by pairing her with producer Glen Ballard. Their creative chemistry was described as "damn close to perfect," leading to a prolific period of songwriting over approximately a year, resulting in music that leaned more towards post-grunge. "Despite two flops, Alannas's publishing company had great faith in her and matched her up with Ballard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Grunge Era Presence
podcast.body: Alanis Morissette was among the artists who maintained a presence on alternative playlists even as guitar-centric music dominated the scene, demonstrating that there was still room for diverse sounds and female artists. "Yes, there were still acts like the Beastie Boys and the Chili Peppers and Ministry and Alannis Moore said, but the primary focus remained guitar music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reinvention and Success
podcast.body: After previous attempts at being a pop star, Alanis Morissette completely remade herself, moving to Los Angeles, finding new collaborators, and embracing a confident, forthright, and angry persona. This pivot into expressing her personal views honestly and directly led to her breakthrough success and status as a trailblazer. "She had completely remade herself. Instead of another fluffy pop song, Alinas had pivoted into being herself and expressing her personal views honestly and directly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Taylor Hawkins as Drummer for "Can't Not" Tour
podcast.body: After the massive success of "Jagged Little Pill" in 1995, Taylor Hawkins, then 23, became Alanis Morissette's drummer for her "Can't Not" tour. He also appeared in several of her music videos and performed with her on her debut appearance on David Letterman. "If you saw her can't not tour, Taylor was the drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transformation from Pop Starlet
podcast.body: Alanis Morissette underwent a dramatic transformation from her earlier, commercially unsuccessful pop albums to emerge as a powerful alt-rock artist. This shift was fueled in part by a personal breakup and a move to Los Angeles, leading to a new musical direction that eschewed "pure pop." "What had happened to transform this woman from a wannabe pop starlet from Ottawa to this woman with one of the angry as breakup songs anyone has ever heard?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins Joins the Band (1997)
xref.body: On March 18, 1997, it was officially announced that Taylor Hawkins was joining the Foo Fighters. He transitioned from being the drummer for Alanis Morissette, who at the time was a bigger act, to an up-and-coming rock band featuring the former Nirvana drummer, Dave Grohl. "So on March 18th, 1997, it was announced that Taylor was officially a food fighter."

xref.title: Comparison to Other Female Artists (1990s)
xref.body: Unlike artists such as Alanis Morissette, Liz Phair, and Courtney Love, Sinead O'Connor was viewed as too intense to be "contained and marketed and categorized." Her fierce independence and uncompromising nature set her apart, and her influence in the 1990s was widespread. "Unlike, say, Alanis Morissette, Liz Fair, Courtney Love, and a few others, Shanade could never be contained and marketed and categorized."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Context of Female Singers Era
xref.body: Her career coincided with an era characterized by a wave of angry and empowered young female singers, placing her alongside artists like Alanis Morissette, Shirley Manson, Fiona Apple, Meredith Brooks, and Courtney Love. "That was an era of angry, empowered young female singers. Think Alannas Morseh. There was Shirley Manson, Fiona Apple, Meredith Brooks, Courtney Love, and Holly was part of all that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career Pressure
xref.body: Radiohead faced significant pressure early in their career, being labeled as potential "one-hit wonders" after the success of "Creep." They overcame this with the help of producer John Leckie and a tour opening for Alanis Morissette. "But this is exactly the sort of thing radiohead faced earlier in their career."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Flea's Studio Work
xref.body: Flea is considered one of the greatest bass players in the world, leading to his hiring as a studio musician for diverse artists including Alanis Morissette, Mick Jagger, and Johnny Cash. He also played bass on Young MC's hit "Busta Move." "He is so good that he has been hired as a studio musician by everyone from Alannis Morse set to Mick Jagger to Johnny Cash."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Following Alanis Morissette's Path
xref.body: Meredith Brooks is described as following in the "balsey angry footsteps" of Alanis Morissette, indicating a similar style or thematic approach in her music. "Meredith Brooks, who followed in the Balsey angry footsteps of Alanis Morissette."

She has also been compared to Alanis Morissette and Courtney Love, being called the "millennial equivalent" to these influential figures. "Others have called her the millennial equivalent to Alannis Morsehset and Courtney Love."

Alanis eventually asked him when he was going to quit and join the Foo Fighters, which he did, despite Alanis being a bigger act at the time. "It got to the point where Alannis asked, when are you just going to quit and join the food fighters?"
